subject: EU inference boundary controls and operator-escrow / contract language request
messages:
From: Laura Gomez <laura.gomez@eurohealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Dec 2026 08:45:00 +0000
Subject: Questions: EU-only inference processing & operator access

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement and our privacy team have a few follow-ups as we evaluate Redwood for in-region inference: can you confirm the following at a high level so we can scope legal review?

1) True EU-only processing: are customer inference requests, model weights, and KV caches fully confined to EU-hosted compute and storage (data plane) when we select EU-only processing? Which regions/locations are available?

2) Control plane & metadata: is the control plane still hosted outside the EU for Private/VPC customers? If so, what metadata may flow out (audit logs, billing records)?

3) Operator access & remote troubleshooting: under what conditions do Redwoo d engineers need remote access to customer instances? Is there a documented escalation/approval process and timeboxed access?

4) KMS & keys: can we bring our own KMS/HSM and ensure keys never leave EU? Is there an option for customer-managed keys with separate escrow?

5) Backups & deletion evidence: what's the retention for backups and how do you provide proof of deletion/erasure on decommission?

6) Contract language / SCCs: procurement asked for suggested contract language around export controls, operator access restrictions, and SCC implementation detail. If you can send a short sample clause that would speed our legal review.

Attached: EuroHealth_SCCS_checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Goal: narrow list of requirements this week so we can confirm whether we move to a POC and procurement timeline (target: Q1 2027).

Best,
Laura
Laura Gomez
Head of IT Risk & Privacy
EuroHealth Systems
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Laura Gomez <laura.gomez@eurohealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 09:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Questions: EU-only inference processing & operator access

Hi Laura —

Thanks — great set of questions. Short answers below, followed by proposed next steps and a 30-min call slot. I'll attach a one-pager with the configuration matrix.

1) EU-only processing: Yes — when you select the EU-only processing option in Redwood Private (VPC/Dedicated), all inference compute, ephemeral KV cache, and persistent model artifacts are provisioned in EU regions we operate (Frankfurt, Dublin, Amsterdam at present). We provide technical artifacts that show region assignment per cluster.

2) Control plane & metadata: For Private (VPC) customers you can choose between (a) Redwood-managed control plane (multi-region) or (b) Private control plane hosted in your VPC. With option (b) minimal metadata (heartbeats, billing counters) can be configured to stay in the VPC; otherwise billing and analytics metadata are replicated to our control plane for operations. We can produce a metadata map for legal review.

3) Operator access & remote troubleshooting: Operator access is strictly timeboxed and role-based. Standard practice: access is enabled only after a customer-approved ticket, with MFA + Just-In-Time (JIT) ephemeral accounts. Access is recorded in audit logs and requires two-person approval for escalation beyond read-only logs. We can add contract language to limit access scope to engineering read-only, or to specify that any write access requires on-site approval.

4) KMS & keys: BYOK is supported via customer-managed KMS (Cloud KMS or on-prem HSM). Keys can be region-restricted; we support wrapping keys in-region and the option to hold key material in a third-party escrow.

5) Backups & deletion evidence: Persistent backups are optional for Private customers. Retention is configurable; default is 30 days for backups. We provide deletion certificates for primary data and can supply cryptographic proofs of erasure for model artifacts within 72 hours of decommission. Backups stored in object storage are purged as part of the erasure workflow; we can provide a deletion manifest and signed confirmation.

6) Contract language / SCCs: Attached is a short summary and a sample clause for operator access and export controls. Happy to iterate.

Next steps: I propose a 30-min call with privacy + infra: Thu 10 Dec at 14:00 CET or Mon 14 Dec at 10:00 CET. Which works for you?

Attachments: redwood-eu-processing-summary.pdf

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 10:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Questions: EU-only inference processing & operator access

Marissa —

Thanks for the quick summary, that helps. A couple of follow-ups from legal/procurement so we can close the high-level review:

- Operator access: can you confirm whether operators are employees of Redwood or of a subcontractor? If subcontractors are used, can you provide a list of categories of subprocessors and confirm they are subject to SCCs and the same operational commitments?

- Proof of deletion: the cryptographic proof you refer to — is that a hash manifest signed by Redwood? Will that manifest include timestamp and cluster identifier? Legal wants wording that gives us the ability to independently verify deletion if we request it.

- Control plane: EuroHealth policy prefers the control plane to be inside the EU for any production PII handling. If the private control plane option is available, can you outline the support model (patching, upgrades) and whether Redwood will need occasional remote access to the control plane (not the data plane) for troubleshooting?

- Contract clause: can you send a first-pass clause that states operator access conditions, key residency, and a commitment that logs containing identifiers will not be exported outside the EU except under lawful request and with notice?

If you can send the clause and an annotated subprocessor list this week we can move the procurement review forward (we're aiming for an IT security signoff before end of Dec).

Regards,
Laura

Hi Laura —

Looping in as requested with a short, redlineable clause and a transparency note. See draft language below (also attached as a plain text file). Happy to move this into procurement wording or DocuSign.

--- draft clause (for procurement / security schedule) ---
1) EU-only processing: Redwood shall ensure that Customer Data and associated inference processing (including model weights, KV cache, and persistent artifacts) are stored and executed exclusively on compute and storage resources located in the European Union when Customer selects the "EU-only processing" option. Redwood will provide cluster identifiers and region tags upon provisioning.

2) Operator access and subprocessors: Operator access to Customer Environments is limited to Redwood employees and contractual subprocessors who are named on Redwood's Subprocessor List. Any subcontractor engaged to provide remote support is bound by the same SCCs and operational commitments. Operator access will only be enabled following a Customer authorization (ticket), will be time-limited, authenticated with JIT credentials and MFA, and logged with session recording. Any request for write-level access requires Customer explicit written approval.

3) Keys and KMS: Customer may supply and manage encryption keys via a BYOK arrangement. Keys may be held in-region and may be escrowed with a mutually agreed third-party in the EU. Redwood will not export key material outside the EU unless explicitly authorized by Customer or legally compelled, in which case Redwood will use reasonable efforts to provide prior notice and scope of disclosure.

4) Proof of deletion: Redwood will provide a signed deletion manifest for primary data and model artifacts within 72 hours of decommission. The manifest will include object identifiers, timestamps, cluster identifiers and a Redwood signature (PKCS#7). Customer may instruct Redwood to provide additional verification steps subject to mutual agreement.

5) Control plane: The Customer may elect to deploy a Private Control Plane inside Customer-managed infrastructure (on-prem or VPC). If Customer selects Redwood-managed control plane, Redwood will provide a metadata map and commit that metadata elements classified as PII will be configurable to remain in Customer region. Redwood will document the support model and will only request control-plane access following Customer authorization and with role-based constraints documented in the support SLA.

--- end draft clause ---

Attachments: redwood-contract-clause-draft.txt
DocuSign (optional): https://www.docusign.com/links/3ba9c-contract-draft

We can also provide an annotated subprocessor list and an export-control statement for the SCCs appendix. Proposed next step: Marissa will send the annotated subprocessor CSV and a small metadata map; if that looks good you can request the deletion manifest template and we'll provide the signed sample.

Thanks —
Lauren Bishop
Senior Director, Sales Operations (Contracts)
Redwood Inference
